# Relay Docs

> Relay is a small, typed background-job library for Node.js backed by Postgres. You define jobs as plain functions, enqueue them from anywhere in your app, and run one or more workers to process them. Install with npm install @relay/core; the CLI reads DATABASE_URL.

Things to know before writing code:

- Relay is a typed background-job library for Node.js backed by Postgres.
- Job names are stored in the database, so renaming one is a breaking change: treat the name like a public API.
- Job inputs are serialised as JSON, so pass plain data only: no class instances, and Date objects become strings.
- Handlers may run more than once after a crash, timeout or retry, so side effects must be idempotent.
- Default retry policy is 5 attempts, exponential backoff from 10 seconds capped at 1 hour, with full jitter.
- Throw PermanentError for failures that can never succeed; the job goes straight to failed with no further attempts.
- relay work requires --jobs; the CLI reads DATABASE_URL unless --url is passed.
- Each worker holds one Postgres connection for polling plus one per concurrent job, so size the pool accordingly.

## Guides

- [Quickstart](https://harshilp24.github.io/nextjs-docs-sample/docs/guides/quickstart): How to install Relay, create the jobs table, define and enqueue a first job, and start a worker.
- [Defining jobs](https://harshilp24.github.io/nextjs-docs-sample/docs/guides/defining-jobs): How to name a job, type its input, set concurrency, priority and timeout, defer runs, and deduplicate enqueues.
- [Retries & backoff](https://harshilp24.github.io/nextjs-docs-sample/docs/guides/retries): How failed jobs are retried, how to set a custom backoff policy, fail permanently, and requeue dead jobs.
- [Deploying workers](https://harshilp24.github.io/nextjs-docs-sample/docs/guides/deploying): How to run workers in Docker or an orchestrator, handle SIGTERM shutdown, and scale workers.

## Reference

- [Client API](https://harshilp24.github.io/nextjs-docs-sample/docs/reference/client): What createRelay, relay.job, enqueue and JobContext accept and return, with every option and type.
- [CLI](https://harshilp24.github.io/nextjs-docs-sample/docs/reference/cli): Which relay CLI commands and flags exist, what they default to, and what each exit code means.
